evidence.quote: | NetEndOfMonth days -> let endOfMonth = DateOnly(issueDate.Year, issueDate.Month, DateTime.DaysInMonth(...)) ... endOfMonth.AddDays days
| true, days when days > 0 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(NetEndOfMonth days))
| "net-eom" -> closed [ "days"; "kind" ] value |> Result.bind (fun () -> integer "days" value |> Result.map NetEndOfMonth)

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Every new rule is in Tier 1 or Tier 2. The due-date rule and the wording are in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). The record encoding is in Summa.Storage (Tier 2). Form parsing and validation are in the Summa.Web.Engine page transition (Tier 2). The change does not touch Tier 3 or Tier 4 code.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no effects. DateTime.DaysInMonth is a pure calendar calculation, not a clock read. The due date comes from the issue date it is given. Parsing and the storage codec are pure functions.

evidence.quote: | true, days when days > 0 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(NetEndOfMonth days))

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Two facts are restated, but the copies agree. First, the 'Net N EOM' wording is written separately in Documents.termsText and in the audit trail's termsWords instead of one shared formatter. Second, the 1-365 day-range check is copied from the Net branch into the new EOM branch (the Net branch at Accounting.fs:2009 has the same check). It is not defined once in Tier 1.

evidence.quote: | Some day when isDayOfNextMonth day -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))
if isDayOfNextMonth day then Ok(DayOfNextMonth day) else Error ...

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The new rules (the day range, the due-date calculation and the ordinal wording) are defined in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). The Tier 2 storage decoder and the engine's form parser both call isDayOfNextMonth instead of deciding the range themselves. The change does not touch Tier 3 or Tier 4 code.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no effects. The due date is a pure function of the issue date it is given. The ordinal text, the codec and the parser are pure.

evidence.quote: | Some days when days > 0 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(NetEndOfMonth days))

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The new facts each have one definition. isDayOfNextMonth (the 1-28 range) is used by both the storage decoder and the parser, and dayOfNextMonthText (the wording) is used by both termsText and termsWords. But the change rewrites the EOM parsing branch and keeps a copy of the 1-365 range predicate there; the Net branch still has the same predicate. The copies agree but are not shared.
